text:
The scoreboard in San Jose looked like a rout, but for two periods it was anything but. Edmonton led 1-0 through 40 minutes on a Mattias Ekholm slap shot from Isaac Howard and Josh Samanski, and the Sharks actually generated the better chances in the second, 0.46 expected goals to 0.20. Then the third period tilted hard. Edmonton piled up 2.38 expected goals to San Jose's 0.66, and the game was settled in about two and a half minutes.

Vasily Podkolzin slapped in a feed from Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard at 3:13, and Alex Formenton backhanded home a pass from Mathieu Joseph and Connor Murphy at 5:40. That made it 3-0, with San Jose's Yaroslav Askarov beaten three times on 2.66 expected goals against. Neither Edmonton goal was a great look (6 and 12 percent chances), which says the Oilers won by volume and territory, not by finishing difficult shots. Tristan Jarry, meanwhile, stopped 19 of 20 and saved slightly more than expected.

Macklin Celebrini cut it to 3-1 at 11:19 on a wrist shot set up by Michael Misa, but the Sharks never got closer. Edmonton took 50 shot attempts to 43 and finished at 3.07 expected goals to 1.28, which means the Oilers deserved to win 77 percent of the time over simulated replays. McDavid was the engine, handling 24 minutes with 2.22 expected goals for against just 0.23 against while he was on the ice, and the shot-on-goal count sat even at 20 apiece.
